absent: Vendor get_feature_msr, set_efer, complete_emulated_msr, cache_reg behavior and full return-code contract beyond delegation points.
Full advertised MSR set, filter creation and default_allow management, and x2APIC exemption rationale beyond range check.
MMU role bits definition, reset context effects, paging detection, and LMA update path outside EFER setter.
PMU mediation, PMC bitmap layout, LAPIC kernel mode and fast ICR and TSC-deadline internals, and instruction skip mechanics.
Guest FPU lifecycle, SHSTK and IBT capability establishment, and host MSR access fault handling for xstate MSRs.
Paravirtual clock cache activation, master and global clock update handling, time-scale computation, and guest memory IO failure paths.
Userspace MSR exit protocol, mask configuration, ignored-MSR global controls, and logging rate-limit behavior.

findings.text: Arch capability query exposes a guest-visible mask derived from host capabilities intersected with supported set, then adjusted for huge-page behavior, L1TF flush mode, absence of meltdown, store bypass, MDS, RFDS and ITS bugs, RTM and TAA and TSX control interaction, and GDS mitigation state.

Supported arch capability membership comprises RDCL_NO, IBRS_ALL, RSBA, SKIP_VMENTRY_L1DFLUSH, SSB_NO, MDS_NO, PSCHANGE_MC_NO, TSX_CTRL_MSR, TAA_NO, SBDR_SSDP_NO, FBSDP_NO, PSDP_NO, FB_CLEAR, RRSBA, PBRSB_NO, GDS_NO, RFDS_NO, RFDS_CLEAR, BHI_NO and ITS_NO.

Feature MSR read entry serves arch capabilities, perf capabilities, platform info with CPUID fault indication, and microcode revision through safe host read, delegating all other indices to vendor hook and expecting host-initiated use.

Common MSR access wrapper clears result on failed reads, passes through statuses other than unsupported, permits host-initiated zero-value reads and zero writes to advertised MSRs, otherwise reports unhandled access when strict or optionally logs ignored access and suppresses the error when tolerant.

EFER validity requires containment within supported bits and requires guest CPU capability for each requested AUTOIBRS, FFXSR, SVME, LME or LMA, and NX feature, mapped to AUTOIBRS, FXSR_OPT, SVM, LM and NX respectively.

EFER update rejects unsupported bits, enforces guest validation and forbids LME change under paging for guest-initiated writes, preserves current LMA, delegates to vendor setter, resets MMU context when role bits change, and warns on SVME without XSAVES support.

MSR filter check bypasses the x2APIC range, then holds SRCU read lock while dereferencing per-VM filter, defaults to allow when absent, otherwise scans ranges for index containment plus direction match and tests bitmap membership before unlocking.

Guest MSR read and write emulation first applies directional filtering and returns filtered status on denial, otherwise routes through ignored-check wrapper around low-level get or set dispatch for guest-initiated accesses.

Fast WRMSR path requires PMU permission based on mediated state and counting intersection, then accepts only x2APIC ICR when LAPIC is in kernel with x2APIC mode and fast write succeeds plus TSC deadline, tracing success and either reentering guest or exiting to userspace based on skip outcome.

General register access masks values to 64 or 32 bits according to guest mode, lazily caches unavailable registers on read, marks written registers dirty, rejects out-of-range indices, and combines or splits EDX and EAX halves for MSR payloads.

Userspace MSR completion propagates returned data into EAX and EDX or nominated immediate destination on success, converts errors into GP injection or vendor completion result, and resumes emulation with no-decode plus skip plus complete-user-exit semantics.

MSR failure classification maps unsupported and filtered outcomes to distinct exit reasons with invalid as fallback, and userspace exit is raised only when the corresponding mask bit is set, initializing exit payload with reason, index, data and completion callback.

RDMSR and WRMSR emulation derive index and payload from ECX and EDX EAX or immediate register operands, trace success or failure, offer failures to userspace when enabled, propagate negative write errors directly, and finish through vendor completion.

Emulator filtered MSR helpers return continue on success, unhandleable on negative errors, IO needed when userspace accepts the fault, and propagate fault otherwise, while internal guest SSP reads use host-style path and other unfiltered reads use direct emulation.

CET-related MSRs are treated as extended-state managed only when guest advertises SHSTK or IBT as appropriate across U_CET and PL0 through PL3 SSP, and their access asserts managed status with active guest FPU state while holding FPU context across host read or write.

Paravirtual wall clock update uses versioned guest memory protocol with odd-even sequencing, skipping null addresses and aborted IO, splitting epoch nanoseconds into seconds and remainder with noted overflow behavior and optional high seconds field before final version increment.

Wall clock epoch prefers master-clock snapshot of TSC and kernel time under sequence protection with same-CPU frequency and time sampling when enabled, computing scaled cycle delta from host time, otherwise falling back to realtime minus KVM clock.

Epoch sampling uses sequence retry around master state, pins current CPU across frequency and wall time sampling, snapshots master cycle and system time plus offset inside the protected window, and performs time-scale arithmetic outside the window.

Observed MSR control data carries index, 64-bit data, host-initiated flag and direction on request side, and exit reason, error, padding, reason, index, data plus completion callback on userspace exit side, with accessor functions taking VCPU, index, data pointer and initiation flag.

Named MSR and exit identifiers observed include ARCH_CAPABILITIES, PERF_CAPABILITIES, PLATFORM_INFO, UCODE_REV, TSC_DEADLINE, APIC ICR offset, CET U_CET and PL0 to PL3 SSP, internal guest SSP, and exit reasons UNKNOWN, FILTER and INVAL with RDMSR and WRMSR exits plus emulator CONTINUE, IO_NEEDED, PROPAGATE_FAULT and UNHANDLEABLE.
Ignoring read failure status without clearing could expose host stack contents to guest or userspace, so wrapper defensively zeroes data on read errors before further handling.

Changing LME while paging is active or allowing guest control of LMA directly risks mode inconsistency, so implementation rejects guest LME transitions under paging and preserves host LMA across updates.

System time registration records old-versus-new clock style for boot VCPU with master-clock update request on change, stores guest address, requests global clock update, and activates or deactivates paravirtual time cache based on enable bit with address masking.

Public helpers used across KVM include arch capability query, EFER validators, MSR allow check, filter-aware and ignored-check read and write emulation, RDMSR and WRMSR plus immediate variants, fastpath handlers, emulator accessors, and wall-clock epoch query.

MSR observability emits directional traced events for successful and failed reads and writes with exception flag distinction, and rate-limited kernel logging for ignored accesses including thread group identity.

Helper completions route through generic instruction emulation without decode and through GP exception queuing with zero error code, while host feature MSR fetch uses common access wrapper in read direction.
